history.summary: Implemented the critique plan: added our-assets-v1.14.1/our-assets/test/run.js, a dependency-free Node regression suite (assert-based, no package.json) that extracts pure-logic function source directly out of index.html via a vm sandbox and runs 15 assertions covering bugs fixed in cycles 0-4 — addMonths month-rollover/leap-year clamping, recDates monthly day-clamp, recNthDate/recCountUntil weekend-adjustment round-trip, num()'s sign-stripping, doRenameCat's catVar/catIcon migration, and activeRecsForAssets. Sanity-checked the harness by reintroducing the old buggy addMonths into a scratch copy — 3 of 15 tests correctly failed, confirming it actually catches regressions. All 15 pass against the real index.html.

Implemented the banked candidate from cycle 4's critique: assetSubline() was rounding fractional a.fxAmount/a.stockQty to integers via comma() (Math.round), while assetEval() already uses the unrounded values for net-worth totals — so a holding like 0.5주 or USD 123.45 would silently show as 0주/USD 123 in the asset list despite the true value being counted correctly in 총자산. Added commaQty(n): integers via comma(), non-integers via toLocaleString with maximumFractionDigits:4, matching how a.goldDon was already shown unrounded. Used it in assetSubline() for fxAmount/stockQty. Bumped APP_VERSION 1.17.2→1.17.3 and sw.js CACHE v37→v38.

Reviewed commit 426cb47 (commaQty display fix) — this exact fix was independently implemented in parallel by two concurrent app-evolve runs (the cloud routine and a local run), both picking up the same banked candidate from cycle 4's critique notes at nearly the same time. Reconciled via `git merge origin/main` (not reset, to avoid discarding either side's work): kept origin's already-pushed commaQty()/assetSubline() implementation as canonical (functionally identical to the local duplicate, only a trivial difference in how the null/undefined case is normalized), and merged in the genuinely additive part of the local work that origin's version didn't have — regression test coverage. While wiring commaQty into test/run.js, found and fixed a real, separate bug in the test harness itself: extractConst() preserved the leading 'const ' keyword when extracting from index.html, but Node's vm.runInContext() does not attach top-level const/let bindings to the context object (only function declarations and plain/var-style assignments do) — so anything added via the CONSTS list was silently unreachable as sandbox.<name> even though extraction reported success. Stripped the 'const ' prefix so extracted consts become plain global assignments in the sandbox. Added 'comma' and 'commaQty' to CONSTS and 3 new test cases for commaQty (integer passthrough, decimal precision, null handling). All 18 tests now pass (`node test/run.js`). Lesson for future concurrent-execution cycles: when both a local cron and the cloud routine are running against the same banked candidate list, duplicate work is possible — check `git fetch`/`git log origin/main` immediately before push, and prefer `git merge` over `git reset --hard` to reconcile (the latter is blocked by the permission classifier anyway, and merge is safer regardless).
